A moody, imperfect documentation photograph of a video and light installation in a dark gallery: Three identical tall portrait lightboxes stand in a straight row on low black plinths down the middle of the dark gallery, as one series.

The output is one single photograph, portrait 4:5.

Shot: Camera at chest height, 35mm lens, f/2.8, square to the row. The three lightboxes stand side by side with equal gaps, together filling about 70 percent of the frame width, the middle one on the centre line and sharp; their glow washes the low grid ceiling above in a cool teal-green and lies as soft smears on the black floor; one visitor stands before the left one as a dark silhouette. Visitors appear only as small dark silhouettes, seen from behind against the light, never more than a fraction of the frame; no face or profile shows.

Place: A dark contemporary gallery: black floor, black walls, and a low dropped ceiling of square panels with small recessed spots; the installation is the main light in the room.

Light: The installation glows and its light washes up onto the low panel ceiling, which picks up a soft cool teal-green glow and shows its square grid; the floor and walls stay near black. No other lamps; uneven, natural falloff.

Palette and grade: Cool and dark: deep blacks, a soft muted teal-green cast in the ceiling and air, desaturated; the glowing design faces are clean white with a faint cool tint. The same grade on every image of the collection.

Real: this is a product mockup photograph of an art installation, so the design surface is the hero: it is large in the frame and the camera is close enough that it dominates, the way an exhibition photographer frames the work, never a tiny object in a big room. It is a real photograph made in camera by an art documentation photographer, not a render. The design surface faces the camera almost square-on, within about 15 degrees, so it reads flat and undistorted; its four edges run parallel to the edges of the photograph, a true rectangle, never a trapezoid or keystone; flat things on a table are shot from nearly straight above. Only the objects named in the shot are in frame. The space shows small honest signs of use; the design surface itself is new and clean. The glowing surface is bright and clean, clearly the brightest thing in the frame, without blowing out; its edges and corners stay crisp. No halation, bloom, haze or glow over it.

Design surface: EVERY SCREEN, LIGHTBOX FACE OR PANEL IN THE ROOM IS PLAIN EVENLY LIT WHITE, glowing bright and clean, never blown out, with crisp edges and corners; nothing on any of them.

Finish: Not a perfect image: like a real press photo of a video installation shot in near darkness, slightly soft, low contrast in the shadows, noisy grain, a little compression and softness, imperfect but moody. Never crisp CGI, never polished.

Avoid: a face, chin, lips or profile, any image, photo, face, text or colour on any screen or lightbox, logos, letters or brand names anywhere, warm orange or peach light, any object not named in the shot, a clean, sharp, polished digital look.
